**STEP 1 - Scene:** A single piece of cooked corn on the cob (a round cross-section of an ear, sliced crosswise), on a white square plate. Photographed from directly above (top-down view).

**STEP 2 - Ruler:** The square white plate is roughly 26 cm across its diagonal-to-corner extent when viewed from above; its side length is about 20 cm, so treat it as a ~24 cm wide plate. Plate area is about 3.14 x (12)^2 ≈ 450 cm² (using the effective round-equivalent diameter, roughly 24 cm). The corn piece is about 3.5 cm in diameter (roughly 1/3 of the plate's width-equivalent).

**STEP 3 - Items:** One item: cooked yellow corn (kernels on a cob cross-section, with the white cob core visible). No oil, butter, or sauce is visible.

**STEP 4 - Area:** Corn cross-section covers about 3.5 cm × 3.5 cm ≈ 10 cm², roughly 2% of the plate area (~450 cm²).

**STEP 5 - Volume:** The piece is a short cylinder of corn, about 3.5 cm diameter and about 3 cm tall. Volume ≈ 3.14 × (1.75)² × 3 ≈ 29 ml (gross envelope).

**STEP 6 - Grams:** Corn cob pieces are a dense, cut-vegetable-like item, so bulk density ~0.9 g/ml (the cob core is dense). 29 ml × 0.9 ≈ 26 g.

**STEP 7 - Energy:** Cooked sweet corn ≈ 96 kcal per 100 g. 26 g × 0.96 ≈ 25 kcal.

**STEP 8 - Sanity check:** A single small cob round of about 26 g and roughly 25 kcal is plausible for a thin crosswise slice of corn on the cob, and it is consistent with a small amount visible on a large plate.

**Result:** About 26 g of corn, about 25 kcal.
